More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.summary: When extreme weather events occur, the damage is usually measured in collapsed buildings, damaged roads and flooded homes. But the aftermath also brings a less visible threat. Heatwaves, droughts, erratic rainfall and flash floods, in combination or alone, also reshape the ecology of diseases. They can affect how long pathogens survive, change the distribution of […]

items.summary: Chief Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal , in his capacity as Chancellor of the National Law University (NLU), Jodhpur, has set aside anti-ragging sanctions imposed on a student of the University. Justice Agrawal noted that the only finding against the student was his presence in the room where the incident took place and held that no proper or reasonable opportunity was afforded to him to place his case. Chief Justice Sanjay K Agrawal The order came in an appeal by a student under Regulation 9.1(c)(ii) of the University Grants Commission's (UGC) anti-ragging regulations. He challenged the order of the Registrar which followed a UGC helpline complaint, an Anti-Ragging Squad inquiry and an Anti-Ragging Committee finding of ragging under Regulations 3(b), 3(g), 3(h) and 5(b). The order suspended him from the hostel for a year, debarred him from representing the University in 2026-27, restricted his sports, cultural and library access, and barred contact with the complainant or witnesses. items.title: How a law student built a tool to track Bombay High Court cases
items.summary: A 3rd year law student from Thane has built a tool that downloads every order in a Bombay High Court case using just its CNR number. Vishal Shantaram Shirsat studies at Smt Smita Ravindra Ghodvinde Law College. He says, "I know what it is to stand in a queue to file something, to ask around for legal aid and to come back on the date given only to find that the matter never came on board. I know what it is to wait for a notice that was not served on time and to wonder who is actually responsible when it is not. For a long time, my answer to all this was patience and a lot of running around. Then I decided to build something small that would at least take one burden off my shoulders," Shirsat told Bar & Bench . The tool needs only the CNR - the unique number given to every case on the eCourts system. It then finds the case on the Court's website and downloads every order in about a minute. Each file is renamed by date and saved in a folder named with the case number and CNR. Doing this manually once took him nearly an hour. Shirsat says that downloading orders is only half the problem. items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday reserved its verdict on the maintainability of appeals challenging a single-judge order directing the registration of an FIR against CPI(M) leader and former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena Thaikkandiyil, her husband Mohammed Riyas and others in the CMRL-Exalogic case [ Pinarayi Vijayan v Adv KM Shajahan & ors ]. A Division Bench of Justice K Natarajan and Justice Johnson John heard the matter today. Notably, the appellants (Vijayan, Veena, Riyas and others) were not parties to the writ petition in which the single-judge's October 9 order was passed. Therefore, a question arose as to whether they can be given permission to challenge a judgment in a case to which they were not parties. All the appellants have filed applications seeking the Court's permission to make detailed arguments in their main appeals. The Court today reserved its verdict on this aspect of whether their applications seeking leave to appeal should be allowed. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed an appeal filed by public sector undertaking MMTC Limited challenging the approval of a ₹1,950 crore settlement scheme proposed to resolve creditors' claims arising from the 2013 National Spot Exchange Limited (NSEL) payment default. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe dismissed the appeal against a March 30 judgment of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), which had refused to interfere with the approval granted to the scheme by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Mumbai. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The settlement scheme, approved by the NCLT on November 28, 2025, seeks to settle claims of specified creditors arising from the August 2013 payment default at NSEL. MMTC challenged the scheme on the grounds that it was prejudicial to public interest and contrary to public policy. The NCLAT, comprising Judicial Member Justice Yogesh Khanna and Technical Member Ajai Das Mehrotra, rejected MMTC's appeal after noting that the scheme had received the approval of more than 90 per cent of creditors. items.title: Emerald Heights International School moves Supreme Court seeking curbs on children's social media use
items.summary: Emerald Heights International School and its Director Siddharth Singh have moved the Supreme Court seeking restrictions on children's use of social media and an enforceable regulatory framework to protect them from online harms. The petition contends that protecting children from environments detrimental to their health, dignity and development is a constitutional responsibility of the State, and cannot be left solely to parental supervision or corporate goodwill. It has sought a direction to the Central government to frame, notify and operationalise a dedicated, comprehensive and enforceable regulatory framework to protect children on social media platforms. Alternatively, the plea seeks a prohibition on social media use by children below a prescribed age and regulation of use above that age, or enforceable age-based restrictions on children's accounts on designated platforms. The plea has invoked Article 39(f) of the Constitution, which directs the State to ensure that children develop in a healthy manner and in conditions of freedom and dignity. items.title: Compensation is not ‘consideration’ - GST on liquidated damages, penalties and forfeiture
items.summary: Between 2018 and 2022, numerous show cause notices were issued by the GST Department treating liquidated damages ( ‘LD’ )and forfeited deposits as ‘consideration’ for having "agreed to tolerate an act" under paragraph 5 (e) of Schedule II to the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 ( “Schedule” ). On Augusy 3, 2022, such view was ultimately remodelled by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs ( “CBIC” ) vide Circular No. 178/10/2022-GST ( “the Circular” )which was issued after the 47 th GST Council meeting under the chairmanship of Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. Demands nonetheless continue, largely because paragraph 12 of the Circular states that taxability in each case depends on its facts and circumstances. As such, it acts like a caveat that facts would be required to be examined and that it does not permit the Circular to be ignored. Where the facts show nothing more than compensation for a breach, the Circular binds the Department. items.title: HNLU to establish International Arbitration and Mediation Institute
items.summary: Hidayatullah National Law University (HNLU), Raipur, has announced plans to establish an International Arbitration and Mediation Institute on the university campus. The plan was announced at the conclusion of a two-day International Conference on International Arbitration held on October 10 and 11. The conference, themed “Governing Disputes: International Law, Treaty Frameworks & Commercial Arbitration,” aimed to advance academic and professional discourse on contemporary issues related to international law, treaty frameworks, and commercial arbitration. HNLU Vice-Chancellor Prof VC Vivekanandan made the announcement during a media interaction on the concluding day of the conference. A budget of ₹30 crore is proposed for the establishment of the proposed HNLU International Arbitration and Mediation Institute (HIAMI) . It is planned to be launched during HNLU's Silver Jubilee year in early 2028. The conference was organized by the Center for Commercial Arbitration within the School of Law and Business and the Center for International Law and Diplomacy within the School of Law and Governance. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday refused to quash criminal proceedings against four youths accused of circulating an obscene video targetting a woman assistant professor. Justice Suraj Govindaraj also made strong observations on the seriousness of the allegations, while dismissing petitions filed by the accused seeking to quash the case against them. “These (allegations) are (more) serious than IPC 302 (murder),” the Court observed. Justice Suraj Govindraj The case involved allegations that a woman lecturer’s photograph and Instagram handle were circulated along with an erotic and obscene video in various WhatsApp groups, including a group named ‘Bad Boys’. The Court noted that this affected her reputation, particularly since the content was shared in the locality where she worked. The woman worked as an assistant professor at a private college in Puttur. Unknown persons allegedly circulated an obscene video in a WhatsApp group, along with details of her Instagram handle and her photograph. items.title: Misbehaviour with lawyer discharging duty is contempt of court: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Monday observed that any misbehavior with lawyer in connection with court proceedings will amount to contempt of court as they are officers of the Court [Sachin Yadav v State of UP] Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal made the observation while dealing with a case in which the PRO of a Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) was accused of misbehaving with a government counsel over phone. "Whenever they [government counsel] inform to any officer about the compliance of the order of this Court, they are discharging their duty in compliance of the order of the Court and misbehaving with them by any officer may be the top-most officer of the State will amount to contempt," the Court said. Considering that PRO Rajesh Kumar Singh had misbehaved with Additional Government Advocate Anurag Pandey when he was trying to inform him about court's orders in a bail matter, the bench ordered that Singh be kept in the Court's custody till 5 PM. "This Court instead of passing any stricture against him, directs that he be taken into custody and he will remain in the custody of court till 5 pm, whereafter he shall be released," it said. He said the right to peaceful protest was fundamental to democracy and must be “respected, protected and never suppressed”. “I have issued instructions to the police to ensure that no peaceful demonstration is disrupted,” he said, while appealing to protesters to cooperate with the police and inform authorities about their plans to ensure their safety and protect the rights of others. “The police are here to protect your rights, not to stand in the way of your voice. The respondents in the case are the Union home ministry, the Delhi government and the police commissioner of Delhi. The plea was filed Monday, October 12, after journalists were seen being dragged by the neck, shoved into buses for no apparent reason, stopped from doing their work, and ignored them when they showed their work IDs , says the petition. items.summary: A plea has been filed before the Supreme Court seeking safeguards for women journalists who were allegedly sexually harassed and manhandled by Delhi Police personnel while covering protests in the national capital. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana agreed to list the petition along with other cases arising from the protests on Thursday, October 15. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Senior advocate Indira Jaising , appearing in the matter, told the Court that the petition specifically concerned women journalists who had allegedly faced sexual harassment while covering the protests. "This pertains specifically to women journalists facing sexual harassment during the course of protests. May it be put on the same date as the other petitions?" submitted Jaising. She further informed the Bench that she had already given advance notice to Solicitor General Tushar Mehta regarding the plea. Taking note of the submissions, CJI Kant said, "I would like some senior officer to be present here to assist us or to explain."
